I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best here in southern Hebei: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. At my age, I would not take on a complicated mix of crops. Wheat and maize are what I understand, what fits Quzhou County’s climate and water conditions, and what I can manage without needing to learn new techniques or take big market risks. If it is the start of the growing season, then my wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so my job now is to topdress it, irrigate at the key stages, control weeds and disease if they show up, and harvest it on time. Right after wheat harvest, I will seed summer maize as fast as I can, keep fertilizer simple, use fewer passes to save labor, and rely on the crop pattern that gives me stable grain and steady income.
